target: Foss'anche l'ultima cosa che faccio, lo porterò a termine.
english: Even if it were the last thing I do, I'll see it through.
old: Foss'anche + imperfect subjunctive: literary emphatic concessive.
focus: 'Foss'anche' = 'were it even' – literary se-less inversion, foss' is elided fosse; gloss it, drop 'emphatic concessive'.

target: Non fosse stato per te, non ce l'avrei mai fatta.
english: If it hadn't been for you, I would never have made it.
old: Non fosse stato + conditional past: inverted unreal past conditional.
focus: 'Non fosse stato per te' = 'had it not been for you' – Italian drops se and inverts exactly like formal English; make that parallel the hook.

target: Sia come sia, dobbiamo andare avanti.
english: Be that as it may, we must move forward.
old: Sia come sia: fixed concessive with repeated present subjunctive.
focus: 'Sia come sia' is literally 'be it as it be' – frozen subjunctive, the cousin of English 'be that as it may'.

target: Ha assicurato che sarebbe arrivato puntuale alla cerimonia.
english: He assured us that he would arrive on time for the ceremony.
old: "Arrivero" → "sarebbe arrivato" in indirect speech (future → past conditional).
focus: Reported future becomes PAST conditional: arriverò → 'sarebbe arrivato', never arriverebbe; also fix the missing accent (tip has 'Arrivero').

target: A prescindere da ciò che abbiano deciso, noi proseguiremo.
english: Regardless of what they may have decided, we will continue.
old: A prescindere da + subjunctive: formal expression ignoring external factors.
focus: 'A prescindere da' = 'regardless of' – and the open-ended ciò che pushes the verb to subjunctive (abbiano deciso); gloss first.

target: Avesse almeno avuto il coraggio di dirmelo in faccia.
english: If only he had had the courage to tell me to my face.
old: Avesse + past participle: pluperfect subjunctive as desiderative in literary register.
focus: 'Avesse almeno avuto' with no se = 'if only he had' – a bare pluperfect subjunctive voicing regret; plain words, drop 'desiderative'.
'Pur essendo stanco' = 'despite being tired' – pur + gerund squeezes a whole although-clause into two words.
